title: Isaac Newton — The Falling Apple, Rainbow Prism & Universal Gravity (1666–1687)

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One falling apple sparked the wildest question—does the Moon fall too?

lines.speaker: halley
lines.text: Impossible, Newton! What holds the Moon up?

lines.speaker: newton
lines.text: Invisible gravity—every mass pulls every other mass!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next, Newton shot sunlight through a glass prism—splitting white light into seven rainbow colors!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every action triggers an equal, opposite reaction—

lines.speaker: halley
lines.text: Whoa! That steel ball nearly knocked me over!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gravity bends a fall into orbit—uniting falling apples and moons under one law!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Rockets, satellites, Moon landings today—every launch flies on Isaac Newton's laws.
